status.label: Reproduce MWB matrix propagation
status.detail: The UI/device ordering report is actionable for reproduction, but Windows edition is not a demonstrated cause.

next_action.label: Compare accepted and received device matrices
next_action.reason: Determine whether ordering is overwritten during persistence, peer propagation or reconnect.

judgment.rationale: The report supplies a two-PC layout swap that does not change traversal. The public discussion contains only a bot suggestion; the old empty-assignee handled claim was unsupported.
evidence: PowerToys 0.79.0 on Windows 11 Pro/Home reportedly keeps the Pro computer on the left despite swapping layout.
MachineStuff.cs exposes MachineMatrix, sends individual matrix entries in SendMachineMatrix and updates/persists received entries in UpdateMachineMatrix.
Related issue 31017 concerns ordering resets; issue 29279 has a different vertical/UI symptom and does not prove resolution.
The broad MWB tracking issue 51077 is not an implementation for this report.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce on two physical PCs and trace the accepted, persisted and peer-received matrix before designing a synchronization fix.

fix_assessment.rationale: A conditional matrix-state correction is relevant; no targeted linked fix or active ownership evidence covers the report.

proposed_fixes.title: Keep accepted MWB device order consistent across peers
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Unconfirmed: the local accepted matrix may not persist or may be overwritten by peer matrix propagation/reconnect. The reported Pro/Home difference is correlation, not an identified edition-specific code path.
plan: Reproduce a two-machine swap and compare UI order, local MachineMatrix, persisted state and the matrix received by the other PC.
Trace SendMachineMatrix/UpdateMachineMatrix and reconnect processing to identify the first state that diverges.
If peer propagation overwrites a newly accepted order, correct the confirmed update sequencing/commit boundary; if the local accept path is wrong, fix that path instead.
Add tests for reversed pairs, unused matrix slots, reconnect/restart and accepting a layout from either endpoint.
verification: Accepted device order matches actual left/right traversal immediately and after reconnect/restart.
Both PCs display the same accepted matrix.
Two-row and disabled/unused-slot arrangements retain existing behavior.

confidence.rationale: Source identifies the matrix persistence and packet boundaries, but no runtime comparison establishes whether the UI save, peer overwrite or traversal calculation fails.

issue_context.summary: Mouse Without Borders reportedly ignores a two-PC layout reversal, leaving one Windows 11 Pro device always to the left.
known_information: The two Windows editions, PowerToys version and ineffective swap are supplied.
Only a similarity bot commented; there is no concrete linked fix.
The source propagates and persists a shared machine matrix across endpoints.
inferences: A state disagreement is plausible; assigning causation to Windows edition is not supported.
issue_context.analysis: A two-physical-PC reproduction is more useful than generic logs. Related broad tracking and older closed layout reports do not make this issue handled.
initial_investigation: Read the complete body, bot comment and cross-reference timeline.
Inspected MachineMatrix, SendMachineMatrix and UpdateMachineMatrix in MachineStuff.cs.
Compared related layout reports without assuming their fixes cover this case.

actions.label: Review device-order investigation
actions.description: Approve the bounded matrix diagnosis and conditional correction, not an unverified Windows-edition fix.

prerequisites: Use two physical Windows PCs with matching current PowerToys versions and working MWB connectivity.
Record Windows editions, device aliases and the initial matrix; use a development build to trace matrix updates. Do not publish connection keys.
steps: Place PC A left of PC B, accept and confirm traversal.
Swap them in settings on PC A, accept and compare both PCs' UI, persisted matrix and received matrix.
Repeat the swap from PC B.
Reconnect and restart each endpoint separately; record when accepted order first differs from actual traversal.
reproduce.expected_result: The accepted order is propagated consistently and controls traversal regardless of Windows edition.
reproduce.setup_prompt: Prepare two physical MWB-capable PCs on a trusted network, verify baseline connectivity, and capture non-sensitive matrix order before/after each accepted swap. Use aliases rather than real hostnames in shared evidence.
